newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 30.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- GERMAN DISPUTE OVER EMU WORSENS

The rift between the German government and the Bundesbank, the country's central bank, has intensified after opposition politicians called for the resignation of finance minister Theo Waigel. The resignation call follows the public rejection Wednesday by the Bundesbank of Waigel's plans to revalue Germany's gold and foreign currency reserves.
-- OFGAS TO PROBE GOLDFISH RIVALS

Gas industry regulator Ofgas is expected to launch an inquiry soon into the 'Goldfish' credit card scheme launched last year by Centrica, the demerged gas supply arm of British Gas. The investigation centres on possible anti-competitive and discriminatory elements to the credit card, which was launched in association with HFC Bank. The probe will be the first by Ofgas into non-gas related activities of Centrica.
-- TELEKOM SEEKS STRATEGIC INVESTOR

German telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom has said it is seeking a strategic investor such as France Telecom or Sprint of the US. Such a move, designed to raise funds without the company having to go to the markets so soon after last December's 7.12 billion stg partial privatisation, could also aid the German government's budget deficit problems ahead of European economic and monetary union.
-- SURPRISE AS TRADE DEFICIT SHRINKS

Figures released Thursday reveal that the UK's global trade deficit narrowed to 670 million stg in March, 90 million stg lower than in February. However, the figures were accompanied by warnings from banks and businesses that the UK economy would be unable to sustain the strong export performance which helped narrow the deficit.
-- ELECTRICITY MARKET MIGHT NOT OPEN UNTIL 1999

Details released by electricity industry regulator Professor Stephen Littlechild reveal that only three of Britain's 14 electricity companies will be ready for deregulation by next April. Although Littlechild said he was not disappointed by the lack of readiness among the companies, it is possible now that full market opening may only be achieved by March 1999.
-- TIMETABLE FOR GAS SUPPLY ROLL-OUT SET TO SLIP

Executives in the gas industry have suggested that the October target date for the introduction of gas competition for 2.5 million customers in Scotland and northeast England is set to be delayed. The October date was set last March by then Trade Secretary Ian Lang, who gave industry regulator Ofgas the option to move beyond the two gas competition test areas in southern England by beginning a phased roll-out of full national competition as early as October 1.
-- NIKE WARNING HITS SPORTSWEAR

US sportswear manufacturer Nike saw its shares fall about 14 per cent in early trading Thursday after the company released a profits warning. Shares across the US athletic sportswear sector tumbled after Nike said its earnings for its current financial quarter, which runs until the end of this month, would be between 51 and 56 cents per share - well below analysts' expectations of 69 cents.
-- AIR FRANCE MAKES FIRST ANNUAL SURPLUS SINCE 1989

France's state-controlled airline Air France has returned to the black for the first time since 1989. Announcing the company's results, Patrice Durand, vice-president finance, said the improvement was primarily attributable to a rise in turnover for the year to March 31 from FFr39.4 billion to FFr42.7 billion. Net profits for the airline were FFr210.6 million, compared to a loss of FFr2.87 billion a year earlier.
-- SEIBE'S 28 PER CENT RISE QUELLS DOUBTS

Engineering company Seibe has reported a 28.1 per cent leap in annual pre-tax profits, from 331.1 million stg to 424.1 million stg. The increase, which prompted the company to dismiss talk of a slowdown in its main businesses, was achieved on turnover of 3 billion stg, up from 2.6 billion stg. Shares in Seibe rose 13p on Thursday, to close at 961.5p.
-- TOSHIBA EXTENDS EUROPEAN PC RANGE

Japanese electronics group Toshiba is to enter the European desktop PC market with the launch of 12 new computer products. Included in the products are the Equium range of business desktop computers and the handbook-sized Libretto portable. Toshiba is the world's leading supplier of portable personal computers and is looking to capitalise in Europe on its strength in the notebook portable PC market.
